To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adoption of machine learning techniques to learn 3D keypoints improves feature matching performance and that our approach is able to outperform the current state-of-the-art.

(1) learning to detect good 3D keypoints improves the end-to-end feature matching performance; (2) the proposed learning framework allows to define both fixed-scale and multi-scale detectors that are descriptor-specific; (3) the performance of the fixed-scale detector is comparable with state-of-the-art methods; (4) the proposed multi-scale detector outperforms state-of-the-art detectors by a considerable margin; (5) the multi-scale detector is able to detect keypoints at different scales, thus

(i) the adoption of learned keypoint detectors, instead of established detectors based on handcrafted saliencies, leads to significantly better matching performance, and that (ii) adaptive-scale detectors, which are able to automatically adapt the keypoint detection scale to local surface geometry, are particularly beneficial for feature matching
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of 3D key-point detection, which can be defined as the task of finding points on the surface of a 3D object that are invariant under rigid transformations and are suitable for establishing correspondences between objects of the same category.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed framework is a viable alternative to the established approach to 2D keypoint detection, where the latter consists in learning to detect good 2D keypoints by optimizing feature matching performance.
we learn to detect good 3D keypoints for a given 3d descriptor.
learning to detect 3D keypoints is more effective than using hand-crafted detectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when it comes to feature matching, 3D keypoints are not a commodity but rather an outcome of the matching process that should be learned together with the descriptor.

, by learning a keypoint detector for each considered 3D descriptor and exploiting the resulting detectors together with the descriptors in an end-to-end pipeline, it is possible to achieve a significant performance boost with respect to the deployment of hand-crafted salient detectors.
learning a keypoint detector is a viable alternative to handcrafting saliency functions, as it allows for optimizing the end-to-end pipeline performance.
